title: PolynomialMixingSubgradient.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: The objective is convex on the closed Euclidean ball of radius R and attains its minimum there. The class permits nonsmooth objectives.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: At a feasible query x, call k returns only the vector g(x,Zₖ). For each fixed x, its mean under the stationary marginal π satisfies the subgradient inequality against every feasible y. This marginal condition allows the conditional mean at an adaptive query to differ from a subgradient. Each call consumes the next path coordinate, including calls whose replies are discarded.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PolynomialMixingSubgradient.lean, spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible and SubgradientOracle.support. LongTails/Template.lean, executeWithTrace and _run

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: For each feasible x, Eπ[‖g(x,Z)‖ᵖ] ≤ Gᵖ with G>0 and 1<p≤2. The bound controls the full reply under the stationary marginal. For p<2 it permits infinite variance.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries and outputs lie in the origin-centered closed ball of radius R>0 in Euclidean d-space, with d a positive integer. All parameters (d,R,G,p,β,τ,ε,δ) are public. The objective, reply map g and path law are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PolynomialMixingSubgradient.lean, Params, Space, Domain, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, spec.Output and spec.admissible

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The real-valued seed path is stationary and absolutely regular. For every n and lag t, the total variation distance between the joint law of (Z₀,…,Zₙ) and the entire tail starting at Zₙ₊ₜ, taken together, and the product of their marginal laws is at most (1+t/τ)^(−β), with β>0 and τ≥1. This condition applies to general stationary processes and permits non-Markov dependence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable feasible point x̂ satisfying f(x̂)−minₓ∈Domain f(x) ≤ ε on the success event, with 0<ε≤GR/8. Any measurable output computed from the final state is eligible.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/PolynomialMixingSubgradient.lean, spec.Output, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm.output and execute

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The success event has probability at least 1−δ for every admissible objective and oracle, with 0<δ≤1/32. Probability is over the oracle path and the independently drawn algorithm seed at a fixed call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines a marginal p-moment subgradient oracle with a single polynomially absolutely regular sample path. Adaptive queries couple the chosen point to the next seed, and the fixed-budget guarantee must control the resulting objective gap at the requested confidence.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Polynomially Mixing Subgradients

We minimize a function f:Rd→R that is convex on a closed Euclidean ball D and attains its minimum there at x⋆, where d is a positive integer. At each query x∈D, the oracle returns a vector driven by the next observation of a stationary, polynomially absolutely regular process. At each fixed x, the reply has a uniformly bounded pth moment for 1<p≤2, and its stationary mean is a subgradient relative to D. For tolerance ε>0 and failure probability δ, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈D satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ.

With ∥⋅∥ denoting the Euclidean norm, the constrained problem is minx∈Df(x),D={x∈Rd:∥x∥≤R}. The algorithm receives d,R,G,p,β,τ,ε,δ, where R>0 is the radius, G>0 is the moment bound in norm units, and β>0 and τ≥1 are the mixing exponent and time scale. The accuracy parameters satisfy 0<ε≤GR/8 and 0<δ≤1/32.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and attainment). For all x,y∈D and s∈[0,1], f((1−s)x+sy)≤(1−s)f(x)+sf(y). There exists x⋆∈D such that f(x⋆)≤f(x) for every x∈D.

Assumption 2 (Polynomial absolute regularity). Let Z=(Zk)k≥0 be the real-valued oracle process, with path law Q on RN0. Write Hn=(Z0,…,Zn) for the past and Fj=(Zj+k)k≥0 for the future starting at j. The process is stationary, so L(Fj)=Q for every j≥0. For all integers n,t≥0, ‖L(Hn,Fn+t)−L(Hn)⊗Q‖TV≤(1+t/τ)−β, where ∥μ−ν∥TV=supB|μ(B)−ν(B)| with the supremum over measurable sets B.

Assumption 3 (Stationary subgradients and moments). At query x∈D on call k, indexed from zero, the oracle returns g(x,Zk) for a jointly measurable map g:D×R→Rd. Let π=L(Z0). For each x∈D, g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under π, and ∥g(x,⋅)∥p is integrable under π. With m(x)=Ez∼π[g(x,z)], we require, for all x,y∈D, Ez∼π[∥g(x,z)∥p]≤Gp,f(x)+⟨m(x),y−x⟩≤f(y).

After the allotted oracle calls, the algorithm must return a measurable D-valued output x¯ satisfying P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε)≥1−δ, where the probability is over the oracle process and the independent randomness of the algorithm.

comparisonHtml:
On the closed radius-R ball in Rd, f is convex and attains its minimum f∗. Each call returns g(x,Zt) from one stationary real stream with past–future absolute regularity coefficient at most (1+t/τ)−β at lag t. The jointly measurable replies have a stationary mean supporting f on the ball and satisfy E∥g(x,Z0)∥p≤Gp at every query point. Here d≥1, R,G>0, 1<p≤2, β>0, τ≥1, 0<ε≤GR/8, and 0<δ≤1/32. The target is a measurable feasible x^ with Pr(f(x^)−f∗≤ε)≥1−δ.

import LongTails.Setups.FiniteSumNondualSmoothConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.PolynomialMixingSubgradient

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  R : ℝ
  hR : 0 ≤ R
  G : ℝ
  p : ℝ
  β : ℝ
  τ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  δ : ℝ

abbrev Space (q : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)

abbrev Domain (q : Params) := Metric.closedBall (0 : Space q) q.R

abbrev Path := ℕ → ℝ

def past (n : ℕ) (z : Path) : Fin n → ℝ := fun i => z i.val

def future (n : ℕ) (z : Path) : Path := fun k => z (n + k)

def AbsolutelyRegular (P : ProbabilityMeasure Path) (τ β : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ t, (P : Measure Path).map (future t) = (P : Measure Path)) ∧
  ∀ n t : ℕ, ∀ B : Set ((Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) × Path), MeasurableSet B →
    |(P : Measure Path).real {z | (past (n + 1) z, future (n + t) z) ∈ B} -
      (((P : Measure Path).map (past (n + 1))).prod (P : Measure Path)).real B| ≤
      (1 + (t : ℝ) / τ) ^ (-β)

structure SubgradientOracle (q : Params) (f : Space q → ℝ)
    (g : Domain q → ℝ → Space q) (π : Measure ℝ) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry g)
  integrable : ∀ x, Integrable (g x) π
  momentIntegrable : ∀ x, Integrable (fun z => ‖g x z‖ ^ q.p) π
  moment : ∀ x, (∫ z, ‖g x z‖ ^ q.p ∂π) ≤ q.G ^ q.p
  support : ∀ x y : Domain q, f x + inner ℝ (∫ z, g x z ∂π) (y.val - x.val) ≤ f y

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := Space q → ℝ
  Query q := Domain q
  Reply q := Space q
  Output q := Domain q
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.d ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.G ∧ 1 < q.p ∧ q.p ≤ 2 ∧
    0 < q.β ∧ 1 ≤ q.τ ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 8 * q.ε ≤ q.G * q.R ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ ≤ 1 / 32
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : Domain q → ℝ → Space q) (P : ProbabilityMeasure Path),
      O = { Seed := fun _ => ℝ, law := P, answer := fun _ (_, x) z => g x z } ∧
      AbsolutelyRegular P q.τ q.β ∧ ConvexOn ℝ (Domain q) f ∧
      (∃ x ∈ Domain q, IsMinOn f (Domain q) x) ∧
      SubgradientOracle q f g ((P : Measure Path).map (fun z => z 0))
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ x ∈ Domain q, IsMinOn f (Domain q) x ∧
      (P : Measure _).real {w | f (output w) - f x ≤ q.ε} ≥ 1 - q.δ

end LongTails.Setups.PolynomialMixingSubgradient
